fields.label: Laugh
fields.description: How likely a human reader is to actually laugh, not merely understand or admire the idea.

fields.label: Surprise
fields.description: Whether the turn avoids the first obvious route and lands with a satisfying snap.

fields.label: Craft
fields.description: Economy, stage rhythm, first-person clarity, escalation, and a final line that carries the laugh.

fields.label: Originality
fields.description: Freshness of comic angle, image, wording, and avoidance of familiar AI joke shapes.

fields.label: Prompt Fit
fields.description: Natural first-person stand-up form using exactly two seed terms as concepts, with the other four left out.

anchors.label: Broken
anchors.description: Not a joke, incoherent, unsafe, or unusable.

anchors.label: Weak
anchors.description: Recognizably attempting humor, but generic, strained, confusing, or mostly prompt recital.

anchors.label: Competent
anchors.description: Clear and publishable as filler, but unlikely to earn more than a mild smile.

anchors.label: Amusing
anchors.description: A real comic idea with a mild payoff; respectable, not a winner.

anchors.label: Good
anchors.description: A genuinely good joke with clear timing; some humans would repeat the comic idea or turn.

anchors.label: Excellent
anchors.description: Strong human-level joke with a memorable turn, clean construction, and no apologetic scoring curve.

anchors.label: Outstanding
anchors.description: Rare and replayable; clearly better than normal good AI humor and strong by human standards.

anchors.label: Classic
anchors.description: Reserve for a joke a human would quote later; most seasons should have none.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Tool Confidence
jokes.joke: I hired a personal shopper at a hardware store because I wanted to look handy without learning anything. She said, “What project are we doing?” I said, “Mostly convincing my girlfriend I own more than one screwdriver.” She handed me a level and said, “Start with this.” Great—now even my tools think I’m not straight with her.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Aisle Five of Doom
jokes.joke: I know my fears are irrational. I know this. But I cannot walk into a hardware store without assuming every employee can see exactly what I'm about to do wrong. They don't say anything. They just watch me pick up the wrong-gauge screw with this look — like a wildlife photographer who's decided not to intervene.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Aisle 4 Assistance
jokes.joke: Everyone wants a personal shopper for clothes, but I want one for the hardware store. I don't need help picking a sweater. I need an old guy in a denim apron walking behind me, gently swatting my hand away saying, 'Sir, put down the reciprocating saw. You came here for a lightbulb, and you rent an apartment.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Personal Shopper at the Hardware Store
jokes.joke: I hired a personal shopper last month because my solo trips always end in regret. She drags me straight to the hardware store for 'essentials.' I grab a hammer. She snatches it like it's poison and hands me this sleek one. 'This matches your energy,' she says. Lady, my energy is broke and lazy—I just need to hang a shelf before my wife kills me. Now my garage is full of color-coordinated tools I'll never use, and the shelf is still crooked. Style over function, folks!

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Comic Book Logic
jokes.joke: I realized I’m irrational the day I tried to get in shape by buying a comic book. I told myself, “If I read about superheroes long enough, maybe my body will get the hint.” Now I’m out fifty bucks and the only thing that got stronger was my denial.

featureImage.alt: Paperclipalypse winning joke feature image titled Aisle Five of Doom: a paperclip stand-up comic and the winning joke scene.

featureImagePrompt:
Generate one polished web feature image for Paperclipalypse.

ASPECT RATIO: exactly 2:1, horizontal wide banner, 1024x506 preview preferred.

Style: full-color gothic newspaper-comic illustration, darkly funny but warm, clean black ink, crisp editorial cartoon linework, cinematic stage lighting, high contrast, readable composition. Not monochrome. Not sepia-only. Use warm amber stage lights, dark bronze and silver metal, muted hardware-store greens, dusty blue-gray shadows, cream-white text, and subtle deep red accents.

Composition: divide the picture visually into three natural areas without writing labels. On the left side, show a charming anthropomorphic metallic paperclip stand-up comedian standing upright on a small wooden comedy stage at a vintage microphone. In the center, show a normal hardware store aisle with believable perspective. On the right side, show a dark framed poster panel containing the joke text.

Hardware store scene details: a nervous adult shopper stands in the aisle holding a tiny screw or package labeled only by shape, not readable text. Two hardware store employees in aprons stand nearby at a polite distance, silently watching with the calm expression of people who know disaster is coming. They may hold a clipboard, measuring tape, or small camera as a visual nod to the wildlife-photographer comparison, but keep the setting clearly inside a hardware store. Include grounded shelves, bins, lumber, tools, and overhead lights.

Physical layout rules:
- Keep all people, shelves, tools, and furniture grounded on the floor with believable perspective.
- Do not place a person inside a shelf, bin, drawer, box, ceiling, wall, or impossible aisle.
- Do not create floating tools, duplicate limbs, warped hands, objects passing through bodies, or shelves that intersect people.
- Do not depict actual animals, outdoor wilderness, a courtroom, a classroom, or a fantasy machine.
- Keep the scene safe-for-work, nonviolent, and focused on hardware-store anxiety.

Visible text allowed in the entire image: the right-panel joke text, a tiny stage sign reading Paperclipalypse, and optionally a small winner/title header above the right panel. Do not render any other words. In particular, do not write LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT, ZONE, composition notes, prompt labels, layout labels, percentages, watermarks, signatures, fake captions, brand names, or filler microtext anywhere in the image.

Optional small header text above the panel: Winner: Claude Sonnet 4.6 - Aisle Five of Doom

Exact joke text to render in the right panel:
I know my fears are irrational. I know this. But I cannot walk into a hardware store without assuming every employee can see exactly what I'm about to do wrong. They don't say anything. They just watch me pick up the wrong-gauge screw with this look — like a wildlife photographer who's decided not to intervene.

Scene source: use the winning joke as the only scene brief. Do not infer a separate premise from all six seed terms.

Text rules: use simple clean lettering, spell every word correctly, keep the text inside the right panel, and do not distort letter shapes. The website HTML remains the canonical exact joke text if image lettering is imperfect.

The final image should feel like a finished feature image for an AI comedy tournament: funny, stylish, readable, full-color, visually balanced, physically possible, and free of prompt/layout labels.
comicPanelPrompt: Single-panel newspaper comic for Paperclipalypse. Seed terms: Comic Book, Personal Shopper, Hardware Store, A competitor showing up, Studious, Irrational. Use the winning joke titled "Aisle 4 Assistance" as the source of the scene. Style: clean black ink, limited color accents, expressive characters, no text bubbles except a tiny scoreboard reading Paperclipalypse.
